target_customer: Banks, fintechs, lenders and insurers that make credit, fraud, onboarding and underwriting decisions
problem: Financial institutions struggle to deploy machine learning in decisions because they lack expertise, IT resources to run ML services, and ways to build regulatory and organizational trust.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS decision platform, sold by contract to financial institutions
product_category: Decision automation and risk decisioning platform

founders.name: Maik Taro Wehmeyer
prior_employers: Custom ML software firm he helped lead (name not given)
previous_startups: Leadership team of a custom machine learning software firm that grew to about 100 people (Index Ventures)
founders.background_notes: Industrial engineering background per the YC page.

founders.name: Maximilian Eber
prior_employers: Custom ML software firm he helped lead (name not given)
education: Harvard (met co-founder there per Index Ventures)
previous_startups: Leadership team of the same custom machine learning software firm
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by Index Ventures and the Series C coverage; the YC page lists only Wehmeyer.

technical_complexity.rationale: A secure, low latency decision engine with model deployment, audit trails and bank integrations for regulated customers, built by a small team in 2020.

defensibility.rationale: Once decision logic and data integrations run in production for a bank, replacing it is costly; certifications also help. Early on, the engine itself was replicable by incumbents or in house teams.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent decisioning vendors existed but no source shows them copying or buying Taktile; it kept raising up to a 2026 Series C.

market_need_then: Index Ventures (Aug 2021) cited that 89 percent of ML projects fail to reach production and that banks lacked ML expertise, IT resources for microservices and regulatory trust, creating demand for a managed decision platform.

identity.logo: Press kit provides logo files; no design description found
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and reassuring, built for regulated environments

brand_strength.rationale: No source shows brand driven growth; the name resembles tactile or Taktile Labs naming noise, and growth came from enterprise sales.

pivots.from: ML and rules decision engine for fintech risk teams
pivots.to: Agentic AI decision platform for financial institutions
pivots.why: Company repositioned its messaging around AI agents (current website and YC page); exact date not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Taktile sold a decision engine to regulated financial institutions, raising a $4.7M seed in 2021, $20M Series A in 2022, $54M Series B in 2025 and a $110M Series C in June 2026, with top tier investors. Success factors are an enterprise sales motion, integration lock in and an AI tailwind; it claims over 200 institutions including Allianz and Monzo. No exit or distress has been reported.
notes: No competitor source dated near mid 2020 was found; present day lists (Provenir, FICO, Scienaptic) come from aggregator pages so the list is left empty. Taktile's site states $80M raised before Series C, search coverage says $79M after Series B; Series C coverage says $184M total versus $189M by simple addition, so totals differ slightly. Seed and Series A press placed the seed in 2021; one Taktile page says Series A was 2022. Series C was announced June 24, 2026.
